articles.title: What is the Stroop effect? When a word gets in the way
articles.queryIntent: A short explanation of the Stroop effect, rather than a diagnosis or online test.

sources.type: Original experimental paper, transcribed by York University
sources.supports: Experiment 2 involved 100 students; conflicting colour words slowed ink-colour naming compared with coloured squares.
Colour-word interference appeared with spoken and keyed responses; other distraction effects differed by task.

claimLimits: No universal slowdown, intelligence score, medical assessment or proven benefit from playing BrainiLab.
The second paper appeared online in 2016 and in the March 2017 journal issue.

articles.title: What is the offside rule in football?
articles.queryIntent: A short explanation of association-football offside, rather than another sport or a rule-change trial.

sources.supports: Position and involvement are separate checks; ball/opponent position, contact timing and direct-restart exceptions matter.

sources.location: Visible What happens if… a player is in an offside position? FAQ
sources.supports: Its visible FAQ distinguishes being in an offside position from committing an offence.

sources.type: Exact-edition official law, same underlying Law 11 as the HTML
sources.location: Printed/PDF pages 109–111, Laws of the Game 2026/27, Law 11
sources.supports: Exact 2026/27 edition of the same Law 11, not an independent source of evidence.

claimLimits: The latest official law was checked on 17 October 2026 against the 2026/27 edition.
The goalkeeper need not be the last opponent; incidental touches do not automatically reset offside.
Rebounds, saves and deliberate-play details are deferred to the full law.
